claim: “In its concessive use, for takes an NP complement beginning with all”, as in [9iv] For all our good intentions, the meeting soon broke up in acrimony.
evidence_summary: Ch. 7 p. 624 [18i] has a content clause instead: For all that I’m not guilty, I’ll still be a suspect in the eyes of history. There “the content clause is clearly licensed by for all”, which is analysed as head, like for fear and on condition.
finding: Medium confidence: §13.2 allows concessive for only an NP complement and makes for the head, while Ch. 7 makes for all the head of a content clause. These are different constructions, so neither statement is strictly false, but §13.2 needs widening and a cross-reference to Ch. 7, §3.2.
inference: Does concessive for take only an NP complement beginning with all?

evidence.passage: §13.2, p. 736. “In its concessive use, for takes an NP complement beginning with all.”
evidence.establishes: A concessive use with a clausal complement, analysed with a different head.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
